newsitem.title: USA: Antec sees $28 million Q1 merger charge.
newsitem.headline: Antec sees $28 million Q1 merger charge.

text.p: ANTEC Corp said Thursday it will take a one-time pre-tax charge of about $28 million in the first quarter of 1997 from costs associated with its merger with TSX Corp.
ANTEC also said it expects combined revenues of the merged companies in the first quarter to approximate the same level that ANTEC reported for the fourth quarter of 1996.

The non-recurring charge covers investment banking, legal, accounting and contractual change of control payments associated with the merger. It also covers integration costs related to facility and operational consolidation and reorganization related to the combining of some manufacturing operations and severance costs from elimination of some jobs.

The charge also includes a writeoff of redundant inventories from overlapping product lines and product development efforts. About $7 million of the charge covers inventory writeoffs and will be reflected as an increase to cost of goods sold which will cut the quarter's gross margins.

"This charge reflects the non-recurring expenses required to combine these two entities and make the operational and personnel changes that will eliminate redundant capabilities and should reduce our combined expenses by approximately 10 percent," said John Egan, ANTEC chairman.

Egan said ANTEC does not expect to see the benefit of synergies from the merger in the first quarter. In addition, purchases of some of its products in the first quarter are expected to be even lower than previously expected, and many product deployments by other customers have yet to begin in earnest, he said.
Egan also said the company expects revenues and earnings to be short of analysts' expectations for the first quarter. These estimates were not available.

Capital spending by some large customers continues at the same reduced levels as experienced in the 1996 fourth quarter, he said. ANTEC is not yet seeing a resumption of robust capital spending for the company's products for system upgrades. Although book to bill ratios for the quarter are positive, ANTEC believes that spending levels by its customers will not improve until late in the second quarter, he said.
